utterances.text: No. No. I'm sorry. I have to tell you. I had to pass by them. You are telling me things that I have to explain to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Bobic, please, we have problems with the interpretation. Please listen to my question and answer quickly with yes or no.

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC
utterances.text: I cannot answer you that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask for the assistance of the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic. You can go ahead and ask if -- like we have been through this before, yes or no, some witnesses say it's not possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I agree, Your Honour. But can we get clarification? Because I cannot even put my question, because the clarification begins before I even complete my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you please now listen to what I am reading to you. I'm reading from your statement, and then I will ask you the question. So paragraph 72 of your statement given in May this year: "I brought all the 12.000 Deutschmarks to him. I had money hidden where they couldn't find it. I paid Brko the money on 12th of December, 1993, in front of the building of the Red Cross." Mrs. Bobic, now I'm asking you: Do you still maintain that you gave the money to Tadic in the corridor of the municipal building?

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Why, then, did you state a month ago that you gave the money in front of the Red Cross building?

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC
utterances.text: That's not true. It could be an error done while the statement was taken.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Ms. Reidy.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm just -- so the Bench is aware that the statement from -- that Mr. Lukic is quoting from was a draft statement that was not read back to the witness. When the witness came here and went to read her statement, those parts which referred directly to the acts of the defendant were -- have been taken out of it, in accordance with the guidelines on the Rule 92 bis statements. So she did not get a chance to re-read those -- this part of the draft statement. She was presented with a statement which she was to sign, which involved all the background information and information that did not -- that would not be admitted under Rule 92 bis. So the Bench is aware what Mr. Lukic is quoting from is a draft statement and he knows that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The draft statement that wasn't signed?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Exactly. A draft statement that was brought back here. It was to be translated and then shown to the witness. Then what happened was there was a ruling in between times about the 92 bis and that, so there will be parts of it the witness has not had a chance to verify, particularly those bits pertaining to the acts --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The accused.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: If there was a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I really have to point to some things, because I do not want to confuse the witness. I merely want to point out to some incorrect facts. This 92 bis statement has not been signed by the witness. The Prosecutor, Ms. Reidy --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... It was intended to be, but it hasn't been, so it isn't a 92 bis statement, because it isn't serving that purpose any more.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I fully agree, Judge Mumba, but this statement was shown to the witness on the 18th of July this year. We received the document from the Prosecution, where the Prosecution indicates certain changes that may have to be done to the statement, but this part is not contained in those corrections. The whole of the statement was shown to the witness, and Ms. Reidy pointed out to the paragraphs which need to be amended. So I don't see any difference between a statement that has been read to the witness and a statement that was gone through in this way. The witness did not want to amend this paragraph. We have a document from the Prosecution indicating that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Ms. Reidy.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: The witness was not shown the whole statement. The Defence do have a document indicating amendments to Mrs. Bobic's statement. That was a statement that she was going to sign as her 92 bis, and it did not have the paragraphs in it relating to the acts of the defendants, because when it was clear that it was -- that those parts of a witness's statement should not be included in a 92 bis statement, they were then removed, and the witness was asked to confirm the background information, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please slow down.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Sorry. The witness was asked to look at the statement that she would have signed and we would have seeked to have it admitted as a 92 bis statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And what you're saying is that those do not contain the acts of the accused?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Exactly, because we had amended to do that. And that's why -- and the information provided to Defence counsel on the 18th of July was the changes the witness had made to the statement that would have been the 92 bis statement had we continued to take evidence under that Rule.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: So I understand where Mr. Lukic is coming from, but it's just -- it was a draft statement, and it's not the case that the witness was shown the whole thing and that's not in my memo that the witness was shown the whole statement. It was just updating them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. But the point that Mr. Lukic is making is clear, that it may have been a draft statement, but that is what was recorded.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: That's right. That's what I recorded in English, the draft statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: But, just again for the sake of clarity for the record, that the witness did not have an opportunity to amend or correct any parts, such as meeting Mr. Tadic in front of the Red Cross building. She was not given the opportunity to read that and other similar passages and make any pertinent corrections. Is that correct, Ms. Reidy?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: That's correct. When the official translation was done, we asked -- we took out those paragraphs so they didn't need to be translated for the purposes of 92 bis.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, on the 18th of July, 2002, we knew, pursuant to the decision rendered by the Trial Chamber, that 92 bis statements would not be used. And on the 18th of July, 2002, the Prosecution submitted a document to me about the amendments that the witness made to the statement. All the statements, all the details, not only pertaining to the accused but to the statement as a whole, were there, and now the Prosecution is trying -- it transpires that the Prosecution did not discuss with this witness anything pertaining to our clients. This is not indicated in this document and this is not something that the Prosecution ever told us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. It's --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Why, then, the amendments? But I will change the topic anyway.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: It's not correct to say that the Prosecution --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may say something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no. Wait. That the Prosecution did not discuss anything pertaining to the activities of your client. They did. What they said is that in the latter statement, after the witness had come here, they removed all those parts relating to the activities of the defendants. No. The point is that the draft which you were given which contains that part which you have been reading to the witness, you don't seem to agree. You are shaking your head. What I'm saying is that the draft you were given by the Prosecution before the witness came was not read back to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we received just one draft. No other draft statement was done where the allegations pertaining to the clients were expunged. Only one draft was done, and this is the draft that this witness was shown by the Prosecution. This is what I'm saying. There is no other draft version. Because at the time when you, as the Trial Chamber, decided that 92 bis statements could not be tendered into evidence, we have not received any other statement from that time on, and this is the only statement we received, and we are prepared to tender it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may say something?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Bobic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I just say how it came about that it is stated here that we were in the Red Cross. The office upstairs in the municipal building, that was the crisis room of the Red Cross, where the gentlemen sat, and we, as individuals, had to go there to be received by them, and not in front of the Red Cross, where there was a mass of people gathered always to wait for a piece of bread that would be handed to them then. Because in the office where this gentleman sat, that was in the municipal building, where it was written on the door "The Red Cross." So he was there in the municipal building, but not in the premises of the Red Cross, where humanitarian aid was distributed. I really have to apologise for being so rude.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Bobic, do you know that Miroslav Tadic never had an office in the municipal building?

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC
utterances.text: It's possible that he didn't have an office there, but he was there in that office. I remember it well. You cannot make me confused in any way, at any time. This is the office where I entered, and I was told that my people didn't want me. Then they calmed me down. I had to talk to them to solve this issue to be exchanged, because I had it up to here of all the hard times that I've had and all the hard forced labour. My child was shaking like a leaf every night, and I didn't have a single pill to help him. I really don't want to walk into -- go into that, because these are some games that you cannot really understand. You don't know what was happening. But this is what was happening in Bosanski Samac. We have to be specific. I'm just an ordinary working person. I am not an official. I do not have a university education. I just want to say in public what was happening.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... silent. I'm afraid this is a criminal trial and counsel has to put questions to you, because his client is facing a serious charge, and I'm afraid you just have to answer those questions. Mr. Lukic, how much more time?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps some ten minutes, not longer than that. But I'm sure that I cannot finish until our working day today, but I don't believe I will go on any further than ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. So we'll have to adjourn and continue tomorrow at 9.00. We will rise now until tomorrow at 0900.
